final_text:
The data cannot identify the organism that caused the sepsis. The plasma report's top non-human species are low-abundance skin commensals, and one of them belongs to a known reagent-contaminant genus.

Non-human species with at least 10 clade reads, by clade count (from `data/plasma.report.gz`, 500,000 read pairs):

| Species | Clade reads | % of reads | Contaminant genus? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cutibacterium acnes | 524 | 0.10 | No |
| Acidovorax sp. JMULE5 | 331 | 0.07 | Yes (acidovorax) |
| Staphylococcus epidermidis | 182 | 0.04 | No |

Why this is "cannot_determine":
- Every top hit is under 0.1% of reads. About 288,500 reads (58%) are unclassified.
- C. acnes and S. epidermidis are common skin and blood-culture contaminants, and the team has no lab confirmation to separate a true pathogen from contamination.
- Acidovorax is on the reagent-contaminant list, so its signal may come from reagents rather than the patient.

I did not use `mockcheck`. Running it with `-I` failed to import the package from this directory, and the question could be answered from the report alone.
